prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals (≤500 words), excluding ideological framing

Health and social care
- Increase NHS revenue funding by about £8bn in year one, rising to £28bn by 2030; at least £20bn capital over five years.
- Reduce waiting lists; rapid GP access (same day for urgent need); universal access to NHS dentists via a new contract and investment up to £3bn/year by 2030.
- Primary care: +£1.5bn/year by 2030; £2bn capital; expand community diagnostics; cut GP admin load.
- Restore public health budgets (+£1.5bn); cross-government prevention; evidence-based drug law reform via a national commission.
- Workforce: fund fair pay settlements; junior doctors’ pay restoration.
- National Cancer Plan focused on prevention, early diagnosis (75% at stages 1–2 by 2028) and publicly funded research.
- Mental health: access to therapies within 28 days; tailored services; a trained, paid counsellor in every school and sixth-form college.
- Support for assisted dying with safeguards; aim to end new HIV transmissions by 2030.

Social care and disability
- Free personal care; rebuild workforce with national pay, training and career structure; invest £20bn/year.
- Protect overseas workers from exploitation; right to an essential care supporter in health/care settings.
- Disability: 5% uplift to disability benefits; oppose replacing PIP cash with vouchers; mandatory free transport for 16–18s with SEND; inclusive housing and workplace support.
- Children’s social care: +£3bn to councils; extend “staying put”; guaranteed counsellor access.

Housing and planning
- Build 150,000 new social homes annually; end no-fault evictions; enable local rent controls.
- Retrofit programme: £29bn for home insulation (towards EPC B), £4bn for public buildings, £9bn for low‑carbon heat, £7bn for overheating adaptation over five years.
- New homes to meet Passivhaus/equivalent, with solar and low‑carbon heating; upgrade PRS minimum to EPC C.
- Empower councils on empty homes and first-refusal purchases; reform planning to require whole‑life carbon assessment, reuse of materials, and reduce car dependence; protect green spaces/Green Belt.

Energy and climate
- No new oil and gas licences; introduce a rising carbon tax; end fossil subsidies.
- Electricity largely from renewables; indicative targets: by 2035, 80GW offshore wind, 53GW onshore wind, 100GW solar; end de‑facto ban on onshore wind.
- Expand grid, storage, interconnectors; develop green hydrogen for industry.
- Increase community ownership; simplify local energy sales; oppose new nuclear and phase out existing plants.
- Skills and transition: invest £4bn/year; create an Offshore Energy and Skills Passport.

Economy, tax and ownership
- Average £40bn/year public investment in a green economic programme (energy, buildings, rail, water/sewage, industry, active travel).
- Bring rail, water and major energy retailers into public ownership.
- Financial sector alignment with net zero: divest fossil assets by 2030; adjust central bank mandate and credit guidance.
- SMEs: regional mutual banks (incl. £10bn capital); £2bn/year in local grants; legislate Prompt Payment.
- Welfare: +£40/week to Universal Credit and legacy benefits; end five‑week wait; abolish two‑child cap; carers’ allowance +10%; scrap sanctions; long‑term aim for UBI.
- Tax: wealth tax (1% >£10m; 2% >£1bn); align CGT and investment income with earnings; remove NI upper earnings limit; reform inheritance tax; stronger windfall taxes; carbon tax from £120/t rising towards £500/t over a decade; anti‑avoidance and more HMRC resources.

Nature, food and animals
- Rights of Nature Act; Clean Air Act; 30% of land and sea effectively protected by 2030; rewet peat; expand woodland; urban biodiversity measures.
- Water companies into public ownership; +£1.5bn to DEFRA; stronger enforcement on river/sea pollution.
- Food: triple farm support to transition to nature‑friendly farming; expand UK horticulture; link payments to lower agrochemical use; free daily school meals and breakfast to Y6; reduce food waste.
- Animal protection commission; ban blood sports; end factory farming practices (cages, routine antibiotics); stricter fishing protections including bans on destructive methods in MPAs.

Education
- £8bn school funding uplift (incl. £2bn for teacher pay); £2.5bn/year to fix unsafe buildings; expand SEND support (+£5bn); restore school nurses and counsellors.
- Early years: £1.4bn/year for Sure Start; extend free childcare to 35 hours from nine months (subject to sector agreement).
- FE/skills: +£3bn for sixth forms; £12bn for FE/lifelong learning; restore EMA.
- HE: scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; address pension cost pressures.
- Curriculum reform; move academies/free schools to local control; remove private schools’ charitable status and apply VAT (SEND places exempt).

Transport
- Raise annual rail and bus subsidies to £10bn by end of parliament; invest £19bn/5 years in public transport and active travel; £2.5bn/year for cycleways/footpaths.
- Rail to public ownership; faster electrification; selective line reopenings; local control of buses.
- Oppose new road building; restore fuel duty escalator; develop privacy‑preserving road pricing.
- Accelerate EV transition: end new ICE sales by 2027; ICE off roads by 2035; scrappage up to £5bn/year; tax by vehicle weight; default 20mph in built‑up areas.
- Aviation: frequent‑flyer levy; no airport expansion; ban domestic flights where rail <3 hours; apply carbon tax to kerosene; support worker transitions.

Democracy, rights and migration
- Proportional representation; repeal voter ID; stronger Electoral Commission; state funding for parties; transparency on lobbying/think‑tank funding; votes at 16; replace House of Lords with elected chamber; more devolution; +£5bn/year to English local government.
- Defend Human Rights Act and ECHR access; restore legal aid; repeal recent restrictions on protest; support self‑ID and X gender markers.
- Migration/asylum: end hostile environment; safe routes; right to work while awaiting decisions; abolish NRPF and the 10‑year route to settlement; minimal detention; split migration from criminal justice; simplify/at‑cost fees; family reunion; NHS access.

Justice and policing
- Prioritise community policing and trust; end routine stop‑and‑search and live facial recognition; diversity competence assessments; more transparent oversight.
- Presumption against custodial sentences under two years; expand diversion and restorative justice; decriminalise personal drug possession with health‑led support.
- Tackle violence against women and girls: classify misogyny as a hate crime; fund support services; nationwide strategy; decriminalise sex work.
- Courts/prisons: restore Ministry of Justice funding (including legal aid), repair courts, recruit judges.

Foreign policy and security
- Support for international law and Ukraine; pursue EU re‑engagement (customs union step, free movement, Erasmus).
- Trade deals without investor–state dispute systems; uphold labour, environmental and animal standards.
- Overseas aid to 1% of GNI by 2033; climate finance to 1.5% incl. loss and damage; debt relief and technology transfer; consider reparatory justice commission.
- Israel/Palestine: immediate bilateral ceasefire, recognition of Palestine, end arms exports, war‑crimes investigations.
- Nuclear policy: sign TPNW, cancel Trident, dismantle nuclear arsenal; work within NATO while advocating reforms and No First Use.
